answer: An identity must lock a bond under a one-per-hardware credential, and each registration emits a quill-signed attestation that independent jurors can recheck. Forging one identity locks 500 units for 20 epochs, and proven forgery slashes 90 percent of that bond. Splitting identities multiplies the 500-unit lock per copy, and a shared karst penalty plus a flagged whisper of duplicate attestations removes any gain.
